A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAPS++ research and contain complete main texts, references, and supplementary material. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment of all content.

before.justification: v2 reports original FFHQ and ImageNet reconstruction experiments in Tables 1–3, alongside efficiency, initialization, phase-retrieval, and hyperparameter analyses in the supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original quantitative experiments and qualitative reconstructions, including the supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The initialization/refinement procedure, Tweedie/RK4 switching, likelihood-only Langevin updates, and re-noising remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same FFHQ/ImageNet restoration tasks and supplementary phase-retrieval scenario. The new footnote pointing to Section S2.2 does not add task coverage; that evaluation already appears in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the benchmark tables, efficiency comparisons, and supplementary analyses. The DAPS-4K phase-retrieval comparison was already present in v2.

E3.justification: Sample counts, image normalization, measurement operators, noise settings, metrics, and computational budgets are unchanged in Section 4 and the supplement. The added footnote supplies no new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical prior-removal, initialization, noise-tolerance, efficiency, phase-retrieval failure, and hyperparameter analyses. Correcting the reference to Fig. S1 introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the mean and standard deviation statistics over 100 FFHQ images in Fig. S2. No seed information, repeated-run counts, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative reconstructions are unchanged, including Tables 1–3, supplementary timing and ablation tables, and phase-retrieval results in Figs. S2–S3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, assumptions, and derivations are unchanged, including the Lipschitz analysis and warm-start convergence arguments in Sections S1.1–S1.3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about decoupled initialization/refinement, reconstruction quality, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 changes 'fully replaced' to 'effectively replaced' without changing the substantive interpretation of the existing evidence. Phase-retrieval limitations and mechanism explanations remain identical; the new footnote merely points to their existing discussion.

D1.justification: Solver and scheduler details, task-specific hyperparameters, hardware, timing information, and resource disclosures are unchanged. The corrected and added internal references provide navigation rather than new technical information.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to existing diffusion solvers remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 softens 'fully replaced' to 'effectively replaced,' corrects 'Appendix Fig. 6' to 'Fig. S1,' and adds a footnote directing readers to Section S2.2 on phase retrieval. The arXiv stamp changes; section organization otherwise remains intact.

P2.justification: The new footnote on PDF page 11 causes limited text reflow across pages 11–14. Figures, tables, captions, and the entire supplementary layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting the initialization-study reference to Fig. S1 and explicitly pointing readers to the existing phase-retrieval discussion improve navigation to supporting evidence and limitations. These are modest editorial gains; the methods, results, and scientific support remain unchanged.
